ei.title: Innovation Lets People Work for Each Other
ei.subject: 11월_2022 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Innovation Lets People Work for Each Other

fullPassage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by enabling people to work for each other. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more specialized in what we produce, and steadily more diversified in what we consume: we move away from unstable self-sufficiency to safer mutual interdependence. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) relying on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to afford to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by (A)[preventing / enabling] people to work for each other. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more (B)[generalized / specialized] in what we produce, and steadily more diversified in what we consume: we move away from unstable self-sufficiency to safer mutual interdependence. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) (C)[relying / avoiding] on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to afford to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① enabling — specialized — relying ←정답
② preventing: 혁신은 사람들이 서로를 위해 일하도록 '가능하게(enabling)' 한다는 흐름이므로 preventing(막는)은 부적절
③ generalized: 우리가 생산하는 것에서 더 '전문화(specialized)'된다고 했으므로 generalized는 부적절
④ avoiding: 다른 사람들이 제공하는 서비스에 '의존하며(relying)' 시간을 보낸다는 맥락이므로 avoiding은 부적절
det.tip: 혁신이 사람들에게 하는 역할, 생산에서의 변화, 서비스에 대한 태도를 파악하세요.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by enabling people to work for each other. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more specialized in what we produce, and steadily more (A)[uniform / diversified] in what we consume: we move away from unstable self-sufficiency to safer (B)[one-sided / mutual] interdependence. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) relying on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to (C)[afford / refuse] to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① uniform: 소비하는 것에서 더 '다양해진다(diversified)'는 흐름이므로 uniform(획일적인)은 부적절
② diversified — mutual — afford ←정답
③ one-sided: 더 안전한 '상호(mutual)' 의존으로 나아간다고 했으므로 one-sided는 부적절
④ refuse: 전등을 켤 '여유가 되도록(afford)' 만들었다는 맥락이므로 refuse는 부적절
det.tip: 소비의 변화, 의존의 성격, 혁신이 가능하게 한 경제적 여유를 파악하세요.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by enabling people to work for each other. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more specialized in what we produce, and steadily more diversified in what we consume: we move away from (A)[stable / unstable] self-sufficiency to (B)[riskier / safer] mutual interdependence. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) relying on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to afford to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so (C)[distant / recent] past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① riskier: '더 안전한(safer)' 상호의존으로 나아간다고 했으므로 riskier는 부적절
② stable, recent: 우리는 '불안정한(unstable)' 자급자족에서 벗어난다고 했으므로 stable은 부적절하고, '그리 멀지 않은(not so distant)' 과거라 했으므로 recent도 부적절
③ unstable — safer — distant ←정답
④ stable: 우리가 '벗어나는(move away from)' 대상은 불안정한 자급자족이므로 stable은 부적절
det.tip: 자급자족의 성격, 상호의존의 방향, 과거를 수식하는 표현을 파악하세요.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by ①<u>enabling</u> people to work for each other. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more ②<u>specialized</u> in what we produce, and steadily more diversified in what we consume: we move away from unstable self-sufficiency to safer mutual interdependence. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) ③<u>avoiding</u> on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to ④<u>afford</u> to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ①가능하게 하는 ②전문화된 ③의존하는→피하는 ④여유가 되다
det.analysis:
① enabling: 서로를 위해 일하도록 가능하게 한다 — 적절
② specialized: 생산에서 전문화된다 — 적절
③ avoiding: 다른 사람들이 제공하는 서비스에 '의존하며(relying)' 72시간을 보낸다는 맥락이므로 avoiding(피하는)은 부적절 ←정답 (원문: relying)
④ afford: 전등을 켤 여유가 되다 — 적절
det.tip: 직접 생산하지 않는 시간을 어떻게 보내는지 파악하세요 — 남의 서비스에 의존합니다.

Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to afford to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by ④<u>wasting</u> and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① diversified: 소비에서 다양해진다 — 적절
② concentrating: 남의 필요를 채우는 데 집중함으로써 — 적절
③ provided: 남이 제공하는 서비스 — 적절
④ wasting: 참기름이나 양기름을 '모아서(collecting)' 정제해 태워야 했다는 맥락이므로 wasting(낭비하는)은 부적절 ←정답 (원문: collecting)
det.tip: 옛날에 등불을 켜려면 기름을 어떻게 해야 했는지 파악하세요 — 모아서 정제했습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:

② serving: 남의 필요를 채우는 것 — 적절

questions.passage:
(A) Innovation enables people to <u>work</u> for each other. Each person serves others' needs for wages, and in return depends on the services others provide.

(B) The old oil lamp was so poorly made that no matter how she cleaned it, it would not <u>work</u> at all and left the whole room dark.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 work의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① (B) 일하다: (B)의 램프는 사람이 아니므로 '일하다'는 부적절
② (A) 작동하다: (A)는 사람이 서로를 위해 '일한다'는 의미이므로 작동하다는 부적절
③ (A) 일하다 — (B) 작동하다 ←정답: (A)는 사람이 '일하다', (B)는 기계(램프)가 '작동하다'
④ (A) 효과가 있다: (A)는 노동을 뜻하므로 '효과가 있다'는 부적절
det.tip: work는 사람이 주어면 '일하다', 기계가 주어면 '작동하다'로 해석합니다.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a situation in which two or more people or things depend on each other"

det.analysis:
① independence: 독립은 서로 의존하지 않는 것이므로 반대
② competition: 경쟁은 다른 의미
③ isolation: 고립은 반대 의미
④ interdependence ←정답: '둘 이상의 사람이나 사물이 서로 의존하는 상황'
det.tip: 'depend on each other'(서로 의존하다)에 주목하세요.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by enabling people to work for each other. You can spend most of your hours relying on the services __________ (provide) to you by other people.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔

(provide) 영어로 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: 다른 사람들에 의해 당신에게 제공되는 서비스
det.analysis: 과거분사 전환: 'the services'를 뒤에서 꾸며주는 자리이고, 서비스가 '제공되는(수동)' 것이므로 동사 provide를 과거분사 provided로 바꾼다. the services (which are) provided to you 구조이다.
det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 '~되는'으로 수동의 뜻을 나타낼 때는 과거분사(p.p.)를 씁니다.

questions.passage: In the past, making light was hard work. You had to make it yourself by __________ (collect) and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔

(collect) 영어로 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 동명사 전환: 전치사 by 다음에는 동사가 올 수 없고 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. 또 뒤의 'and refining'과 병렬 구조이므로 collect도 같은 형태인 collecting으로 바꾼다.
det.tip: 전치사 by 뒤, 그리고 and로 연결된 refining과 짝을 맞추려면 동명사 collecting이 됩니다.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by enabling people to __________. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more specialized in what we produce, and steadily more diversified in what we consume: we move away from unstable self-sufficiency to safer mutual interdependence. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) relying on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to afford to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 서로를 위해 일하다 / 홀로 살다 / 경쟁자와 다투다 / 멀리 여행하다
det.analysis:
① work for each other ←정답: 혁신이 삶을 바꾸는 최선의 방식은 사람들이 '서로를 위해 일하도록' 하는 것이다. 이어지는 내용(전문화·상호의존)이 이를 뒷받침한다
② live all alone: 홀로 사는 것은 글의 상호의존 논지와 반대
③ compete with rivals: 경쟁은 문맥과 무관
④ travel far away: 여행은 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 전문화와 상호의존이라는 글 전체의 주제가 첫 문장의 빈칸을 결정합니다.

questions.passage: The best way in which innovation changes our lives is by enabling people to work for each other. The main theme of human history is that we become steadily more specialized in what we produce, and steadily more diversified in what we consume: we move away from unstable self-sufficiency to safer __________. By concentrating on serving other people's needs for forty hours a week — which we call a job — you can spend the other seventy-two hours (not counting fifty-six hours in bed) relying on the services provided to you by other people. Innovation has made it possible to work for a fraction of a second in order to be able to afford to turn on an electric lamp for an hour, providing the quantity of light that would have required a whole day's work if you had to make it yourself by collecting and refining sesame oil or lamb fat to burn in a simple lamp, as much of humanity did in the not so distant past.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 완전한 독립 / 완전한 고립 / 상호의존 / 개인의 자유
det.analysis:
① total independence: 우리가 향하는 곳은 서로 의존하는 상태이므로 '완전한 독립'은 반대
② complete isolation: 완전한 고립은 반대 의미
③ mutual interdependence ←정답: 우리는 불안정한 자급자족에서 벗어나 더 안전한 '상호의존'으로 나아간다
④ personal freedom: 개인의 자유는 문맥과 무관
det.tip: 'move away from ... self-sufficiency to safer __________'에서 자급자족의 반대 방향을 파악하세요.
